page: Microsoft Azure B20ms is a burstable virtual machine belonging to the BS family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 20 vCPUs mapped to 20 physical cores using an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8272CL processor clocked at 2.6 GHz. The CPU configuration provides 1.0 thread per core and includes a 50 MB L3 cache, 0.25 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache. It is equipped with 80.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes 164 GB of local storage. The instance supports Premium Storage but does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results indicate a distinct performance profile characterized by weak single-core capabilities but average multi-core and memory performance. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance, Geekbench single-core score, and single-threaded compression tasks all fall into the bottom 25% tier. Conversely, multi-core metrics, including stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores, rank in the middle 50%. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks, along with Passmark memory and database operations, also consistently achieve average tiering.

Due to its burstable CPU allocation model, the B20ms is structured for workloads with variable CPU utilization. It delivers qualitative cost efficiency for applications that require a high memory footprint of 80.0 GB and a high core count but do not continuously saturate the CPU. Suitable workloads include database operations, static web serving, and software compilation, which align with its average multi-threaded and database benchmark ratings. However, it is poorly suited for continuous heavy compute or real-time LLM text generation, where its performance drops to the bottom 10% to 25% tiers.
